subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should main-session `systemEvent` cron jobs gain a supported transient model/provider override contract, and if so should that contract be `payload.model`, top-level job fields, or a dedicated override block?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes public cron schema, provider/model precedence, session-state isolation, and upgrade expectations; automation should not pick that API shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Extend `systemEvent` with transient `payload.model`
options.body: Allow `systemEvent` payloads to carry a model ref, validate it through existing allowed-model routing, and thread it as a one-run override through main-session cron heartbeat execution without writing permanent session metadata.

options.title: Add top-level job override fields
options.body: Introduce job-level model/provider fields that apply across payload kinds, accepting a broader cron schema and documentation surface for a more uniform API.

options.title: Keep systemEvent text-only
options.body: Document isolated/current/session `agentTurn` as the supported per-job model path and leave main-session system events tied to the target session's model state.

recommendation.title: Extend `systemEvent` with transient `payload.model`
recommendation.body: Allow `systemEvent` payloads to carry a model ref, validate it through existing allowed-model routing, and thread it as a one-run override through main-session cron heartbeat execution without writing permanent session metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: CONTRIBUTING.md lists Tyler Yust for cron, and this decision is primarily cron product/API direction rather than a narrow code repair.
